content: Verification handoff: docs/reviews/REV-20260811-154157.md (reviewed_files matches e818792 exactly; newest carrier). Re-ran the checker: git diff e818792^ e818792 | verify_paths_not_taken.py --discussion DISC-20260811-210611-i-clear-it-gate-clearing --diff - --json -> exit 1, VERIFICATION FAILED, 14 records, 2 CONTRADICTED, 1 UNRECORDED — reproduces the REV's copied result exactly. Per-claim reader verdicts on the two CONTRADICTED: (turn 16, WIDEN-the-detector) VERIFIED — falsifier KNOWN-UNCAUGHT hits tests/test_education_gate.py:487, a docstring line documenting the register turn 18 created for a DIFFERENT escape set; the widening turn 16 chose exists; the diff does not do what the record rejected. (turn 18, DOCUMENT-not-widen) VERIFIED — falsifier 'gerund arm' hits :491-492, prose explaining WHY the gerund arm was rejected; detector arms verified base-form, no gerund arm exists. Both are FALSE refutations, specimens 3+4 of the checker-loosening class (threshold 2 — /retro item stands). Taught with the gap named, never as clean statuses. Remaining 12 records MECHANICALLY-CLEAR (not promoted to VERIFIED; string-search only). UNRECORDED: selecting-review-gates/SKILL.md 42 lines — covered by correction turn 17, which the coverage proxy does not read; taught as advisory.

EDUCATOR WALKTHROUGH — ADR-0035 "I clear it" (e818792). Three segments, checkpoints + rubrics + unspent entry points per segment. Confidence 0.86. Entering estimates: strategic s-tier-2 (he authored the governing decisions), implementation i-tier-1 (guard layering + marker lifecycle new).

SEGMENT 1 — DECISION LANDSCAPE. The education gate now clears on exactly one action: the developer personally running gate_registry.py clear. Everything upstream (teaching, recording, registering debt) stays automatic; only the closing act does not. Before: two closers, neither him — /quiz instructed the tutor to run clear alongside recording results; the ADR-0029 phone/ingest route computed the formula and called clear_gate() itself. Hazard (named in the registry module docstring): clear_gate validates nothing about the ids it writes — an agent that can clear can produce a tidy registry (zero open debt) measuring the tutor's housekeeping, not comprehension. His three decisions settled it: (1) "I clear it" (ntfy); (2) "Yes, everywhere" — presence in the room ≠ decision in the registry; rule tracks who performs the closing act (declines Alt #1 keep phone auto-clear); (3) Q9 conditions — declined Alt #2 independent grader as "empty governance"; instead per-attempt verbatim capture continues + the gap is WATCHED (retro query). Other alternatives declined: #3 blocking gate (understanding offered, not withheld; authority ≠ chore); #4 wire v2 bump (payload identical; would reject live phone transcripts); #5 report cleared without flipping registry (log would teach a state that never happened); #6 manual re-defer for symmetry (re-defer renews debt, same class as add; manual would strand walked-away sessions); #7 THE PATH BUILT THEN REVERTED — round 1 shipped eligibility as stdout only; review VETOED: a gate quizzed at 0.9 rendered byte-identically to one nobody opened → the additive clear_eligible marker, durable in the registry, validator forbids it on cleared gates. Precedent: the first real clear (EDU-20260810-wave3-sliced, d521a21) was BY HIS HAND before the code enforced it — the code caught up to his practice. Cross-repo: CONTRACTS.md v1.1 formal revision; outcome=cleared → outcome=clear-eligible posted to the changelog board for insight_journal.
CHECKPOINT 1: If presence in the room had justified the old auto-clear, what would still be missing from the registry that only his own clear supplies, and why is it worth one extra step on a gate he knows he passed? Miss traces to: presence-as-observation vs decision-as-recorded-act (cleared_by is provenance of an act, not who was in the room). Unspent entry points on a miss: analogy-from-owned-domain, then failure-mode-first.

SEGMENT 2 — INVARIANTS & FAILURE MODES. Invariant: only clear_gate() may set cleared/cleared_by, and since this change nothing automatic calls it; ingest returns no clearing action and writes mark_clear_eligible instead (status stays open; validator REJECTS the marker on an already-cleared gate). Second deliberate omission: mark_clear_eligible has NO CLI — reachable only from the validated ingest path; a standalone command would be a paste-ready way to mint paid markers with no session behind them. Testing story: three guards against reintroduction — (1) text scanner over agent-facing surfaces for clear/retire wording; (2) test spy counting clear_gate() calls during ingest; (3) behavioral check on a real tmp registry: is the gate still open after? A critic's crafted change FOOLED #1 AND #2 SIMULTANEOUSLY; only #3 (observed outcome) held. Recorded as "layered, not independent" in REV-20260811-154157. Lesson: assertions about intention (wording, call counts) can be worded around; the outcome check is the load-bearing layer. Honest limitations: nothing verifies the grading itself (clear attests HIS act on presented evidence, not the grading's soundness — Q9 gap, watched); registry trusts the ids it is handed (forged clear out of scope); a known lost-update race between his manual paste and the watcher process — atomic write prevents torn files, not lost updates — evaluated and deferred on topology grounds.
CHECKPOINT 2: Given #1+#2 were fooled and only #3 caught it — which guard would he rely on, and why do the other two stay in the suite rather than being deleted? Miss traces to: intention-expressed vs outcome-observed tests; thick-looking coverage can share one blind spot. Unspent entry points: counterfactual (no guard #3 — walk the crafted change through), then losing-alternative's-point-of-view (argue for #1+#2 only).

SEGMENT 3 — DIAGNOSTIC. Gate not clearing: read docs/education/gates.yaml or gate_registry.py list — check status, clear_eligible block, cleared_by; open+marker = "paid, awaiting your clear", not an error. Lost the paste: list --eligible re-prints it durably (pins --registry for non-default files). Old logs: machine summary changed outcome=cleared → outcome=clear-eligible on the same success path — literal matchers on the old string now silently find nothing (the one named cross-repo break). Trusting a marker: it attests a passing session was RECORDED against the locked formula (walkthrough + quiz avg >=0.70 + explain-back); it does NOT attest grading rigor — per-item scores are producer-authoritative; more confidence lives in Layer 1 (sealed transcript) + metrics/evaluation.db education_results (verbatim per-attempt rows). Standing instrument: /retro zero-miss watch (a sustained all-first-ask run = grading possibly soft; informational, read the transcripts before concluding — an easy week looks the same). Checker caveat: the automated verifier returned exit 1 on this very change; both CONTRADICTED were FALSE ALARMS (string matcher cannot tell "about a sibling decision" from "contradicts this one"); specimens 3+4; loosen-the-checker formally owed. Red checker on this class = prompt to read the flagged content, not a verdict.
CHECKPOINT 3: A gate shows clear-eligible with quiz average barely at 0.70 — what can the marker NOT reassure him about, and where would he look for more confidence? Miss traces to: eligible ≠ verified (marker = recorded pass, not sound grading — the system only makes the first claim). Unspent entry points: failure-mode-first, then analogy-from-owned-domain.

Sources: ADR-0035, REV-20260811-154157, CONTRACTS.md §1.4/§4/changelog, DISC-20260811-210611, gate_registry.py (_validate_clear_eligible, mark_clear_eligible, clear_command_for, backlog_summary), ingest_walkthrough_session.py (_decide), test_education_gate.py (check 14, KNOWN_UNCAUGHT_CLEAR_ESCAPES), retro.md (zero-miss watch).

Checkpoint 1 (decision landscape): You told the phone route 'yes, everywhere,' even though you'd personally sat through that session. If your presence in the room had been enough to justify the old auto-clear, what specific thing would still be missing from the registry that only your own clear command supplies — and why does that missing thing matter enough to be worth one extra manual step on a gate you already know you passed?

At checkpoint 1 the developer raised a steer instead of an answer (verbatim): 'I am concerned we are adding too much process around the education gate. I want it to help me understand the code AI wrote, but I don't want it to be a strict gate. I think my intent on saying "clear it" and "yes, everywhere" was to make it less burdensome, not more. For instance, I might go through an education gate that I feel I understand, and I want to "clear it", possibly without the quiz. I am concerned this might turn into an over-engineered process that makes it hard to use this framework, which wasn't my intent. Talk me through this.'

Depth agreement reached with the developer (accepted 2026-08-14): layers 2+3 delivered briefly, quiz skippable if he feels solid, then the clear command is handed to him — his call closes the gate. Checkpoint 1 stands unanswered (he raised the burden steer instead) — recorded as untested ground, not faked as demonstrated. Policy addition accepted for the QUEUED tutor-loop dedup slice spec (nothing changes until his spec approval): walkthrough-only clearing becomes the recognized default for ordinary changes; quiz on request or for the two non-declinable classes.

Checkpoint 2 (invariants): Given that guard 1 (the text scanner) and guard 2 (the call-counting spy) were both fooled by the same crafted change, and only guard 3 (checking the actual resulting gate status) caught it — which of the three would you actually rely on, and why do the other two stay in the suite rather than being deleted as useless?

Checkpoint 2 answer (verbatim): 'The behavioral check (#3) is the one that I rely on at the end of the day. The other two are still useful. Just because an intentional attack that successfully bypassed them happened, it doesn't mean that those guards are not valuable.' Tutor judgment: DEMONSTRATED first ask — correct reliance ordering (outcome-observed over intention-expressed) and the load-bearing insight that adversarial bypass does not zero a guard's value; tutor added one enrichment (guards 1+2 catch honest drift cheaply and point at the offending line; #3 proves breakage but not location) rather than re-teaching.

Checkpoint 3 (diagnostic): A gate shows clear-eligible with a quiz average that just barely cleared the 0.70 threshold. Before you paste the clear command — what does the design say the eligibility marker CANNOT reassure you about, and if you wanted more confidence than the marker gives you, where would you actually go look?

Checkpoint 3 answer (verbatim): 'The marker doesn't tell me how rigorous the grading was behind the formula. You would have to look upstream to see what the formula was.' Tutor judgment: first half DEMONSTRATED (marker cannot attest grading rigor). Second half PARTIAL MISS — 'look at the formula' points at the wrong object: the formula is fixed and was satisfied; rigor lives in the recorded evidence (sealed transcript verbatim answers, education_results rows), not in the rule that was met.
checkpoint miss (partial) on eligible-vs-verified evidence location; re-explaining from entry point failure-mode-first

Checkpoint 3 re-ask (verbatim): 'I would open my actual answers to verify.' Tutor judgment: DEMONSTRATED after one failure-mode-first re-teach — evidence over rule; the verbatim per-attempt answers are the audit surface.

Walkthrough handoff. Demonstrated in his own words (do NOT re-ask): outcome-observed-over-intention-expressed guard reliance incl. why fooled guards stay (checkpoint 2, first ask); eligible-vs-verified with evidence-not-formula as the audit surface (checkpoint 3, after one re-teach). Entry points already spent, per concept: eligible-vs-verified -> failure-mode-first. Layers skipped / untested ground: checkpoint 1 (presence-as-observation vs decision-as-recorded-act) UNANSWERED — the developer raised the burden steer instead (captured turn 4); quiz SKIPPED at the developer's election under the recorded depth agreement (turn 5) — legitimate under Principle #5 and his sovereign clear. Rationale hedged where the decision record was thin: none — ADR-0035 record is dense; the two CONTRADICTED checker statuses were reader-verified FALSE refutations and taught as the gap (turn 1).
